paragraphs: Once everyone was accounted for and we realized we'd all made it, we learned we were on the island of Malta. The locals went out of their way to be kind to us. It was rainy and cold, and we were soaked to the bone — but they built a huge bonfire and gathered us around it.

Paul pitched in to help. He'd gathered an armful of sticks, but when he laid it on the fire, a venomous snake — jolted awake by the heat — sank its fangs into his hand and hung on. Seeing the snake dangling from Paul's hand, the locals jumped to the conclusion that he was a murderer getting what he deserved. Paul just shook the snake off into the fire like it was nothing. They kept waiting for him to keel over dead — but when it became obvious he wasn't going to, they flipped to the opposite conclusion: he must be a god!

The leading man on that part of the island was Publius. He welcomed us into his home as his guests, dried us out, and hosted us in fine style for three days. Publius's father was sick at the time — down with a high fever and dysentery. Paul went into the old man's room, laid hands on him, prayed — and the man was healed. News of the healing spread fast, and soon every sick person on the island came and was healed.

We spent an amazing three months on Malta. They treated us like royalty, met all our needs, and stocked us up for the rest of the journey. When an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the harbor got ready to sail for Italy, we boarded. The ship's figurehead was the twin gods Castor and Pollux — "the Heavenly Twins."

We docked at Syracuse for three days, then sailed up the coast to Rhegium. Two days later, with a south wind behind us, we sailed into the Bay of Naples. We found Christian friends there and stayed with them for a week.

And then we reached Rome. Friends in Rome heard we were coming and came out to meet us. One group came as far as the Forum of Appius; another met us at the Three Taverns — emotional reunions, as you can imagine. Paul, overflowing with praise, led us in prayers of thanksgiving. When we actually entered Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier assigned to guard him.

Three days later, Paul invited the local Jewish leaders to meet at his house. He said, "Fellow Jews, the leaders in Jerusalem arrested me on trumped-up charges, and I ended up in Roman custody. I want you to know I did absolutely nothing against our laws or our customs. After the Romans investigated and found nothing to the charges, they wanted to let me go — but the Jews objected so fiercely that I was forced to appeal to Caesar. I didn't do it to accuse our people of anything or to get them in trouble with Rome — we've had more than enough of that kind of trouble over the years. I did it *for* Israel. I asked you here today to make it clear that I'm on Israel's side, not against her. I'm chained here because of hope, not doom."

They said, "Nobody wrote to warn us about you, and no one has shown up with anything bad to say about you. But we'd really like to hear more. The only thing we know about this Christian movement is that people everywhere seem to speak against it."

They set a date. When the day came, they returned to his house with quite a few friends. Paul talked to them all day long, from morning till evening — explaining everything about the kingdom of God and trying to persuade them about Jesus, pointing to what Moses and the prophets had written about him.

Some were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe a word. When the unbelievers got cranky and started arguing among themselves, Paul cut in: "I have just one more thing to say. The Holy Spirit knew exactly what he was talking about when he spoke to our ancestors through the prophet Isaiah: Go to this people and tell them: 'You will listen with your ears but never understand; you will look with your eyes but never see. These people are stubborn! They plug their ears so they don't have to listen; they shut their eyes so they don't have to look — so they won't have to face me and let me heal them.'"
"You've had your chance. The non-Jewish outsiders are next. And believe me — they're going to welcome it with open arms!"

Paul lived two whole years in his rented house. He welcomed everyone who came to see him. He boldly proclaimed everything about the kingdom of God. He taught all about Jesus Christ. His door was always open.
